architecture_decisions: 4.1 Admission metadata `AdmittedAgent` gains a bounded non-negative integer selection-priority field. The default preserves generic/reference behavior. The value is server admission policy, not part of `AgentIdentity`, but it is serialized into the admitted-roster evidence so changing priority changes the roster digest and therefore plan identity.
work_items: 4.1 Admission metadata `AdmittedAgent` gains a bounded non-negative integer selection-priority field.
validations: 4.1 Admission metadata `AdmittedAgent` gains a bounded non-negative integer selection-priority field.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — For a serial implementation work unit with all three hosted agents equally eligible, the first scheduled model is `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` even when its identity digest does not sort first lexically.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — When Luna is rejected before canonical mutation, candidate recovery selects Terra next; if Terra is also rejected and the existing reassignment bound permits another alternate, Sol is selected last.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — For equivalent-capability work, a one-agent plan selects Luna; a two-agent parallel plan selects Luna and Terra. Sol is not selected merely because of digest order.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — Equivalent graph, roster, priority metadata and policy produce identical roster digest, plan ID and schedule regardless of input tuple ordering.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Changing an admitted agent's selection priority changes admitted-roster evidence/digest and therefore cannot silently alter scheduling under an unchanged plan identity.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Agents with equal selection priority retain deterministic identity-digest tie ordering.
AC-07: validate protected requirement — Duplicate, unknown, malformed or non-admitted selected/eligible digests remain rejected. Priority cannot make an ineligible agent schedulable.
AC-08: validate protected requirement — Candidate recovery remains bounded by `max_reassignments_per_work_unit`; worker process/lease recovery semantics remain unchanged.
AC-09: validate protected requirement — The ordinary non-agentic `ModelRouter` continues to use its existing `Luna -> Terra -> Sol` sequence and no provider/model authority is widened.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Focused orchestration/candidate-recovery tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, protected spec/plan, DSPy release and protected promotion gates pass on exact head. Production runtime evidence after deployment shows a representative autonomous implementation starts with Luna, and a Luna-success path does not call Sol.

critique:
:
- The hosted production-agent selection follows the server-owned cost/capability escalation policy `openai/gpt-5.6-luna -> openai/gpt-5.6-terra -> openai/gpt-5.6-sol` instead of the lexical order of agent identity SHA-256 digests. The selected team order is canonicalized from the priority-ordered admitted roster rather than re-sorted lexically by digest.
